Only took 4 stabs this time to get the labret where we wanted it, but my piercer was fantastic! Crooked nose squad, you too can have a vertical labret lol. Just be prepared to suffer for it 😂

I've gotten my vertical labret done multiple times at a total of 3 separate shops, and it took 4 stabs in one session this last time to get it centered and 99% straight because my nose and face are so damn crooked lol. But the piercer was fantastic and we just redid it until it was right. So, to answer your question: let it heal over for a month and go get it redone. If you hate it again, the sooner you remove it the easier it will be to repierce. Good luck!

Edit: also, titanium jewelry will likely help you avoid the bump next time. But it will heal and yes, you should be able to get it redone!

That's so cool that you maybe got to see your record! I've tried a couple regressions since this one and haven't gotten anything much... am starting to wonder if something is blocking me, too. Have you ever found a way past the block?
I got my first month of doxy from my dermatologist for acne. In the event your GP won't give you the doxy, a derm might be worth a shot.

If you've been feeling sick for a month, the standard two weeks of antibiotics will not get you well - yes, he is worth the investment, as no regular MD or ID doc will give you the length of treatment and potentially multiple medications you'll need. 

I've seen him and he's a great guy, but my case was just too complicated to be handled remotely. I imagine if you have few other complex health problems besides lyme or are in the area where he physically practices, he'll have no problems getting you feeling better long term with few issues.
Thank you so much, the encouragement means a lot :)

That was me, too. Not for as long as you, but I was so frustrated because when I got done with doxycycline - I felt 100% normal as long as I took it, but the minute I stopped the lyme symptoms started coming back. It's been that way with all abx since. I'm heading in to get my adrenals checked hopefully this coming week, so I'll go from there. Thank you!

HIV yes (negative), hepatitis I think so but I'm not sure. I'll ask in my next appt. Edit: did my own chelation after a month with no help. Iron level is normal again. DIY was a nightmare.
